Subject: Re: Geo-lock verification and tenant segregation — technical details and timings

Chris / Priya — adding the technical response and timelines below. Summary first, then sample evidence references.

Summary:
- Region pinning: Dedicated tenant control plane marks the tenant routing key with a single region identifier. Compute and attached volumes are scheduled to hosts in that region. Snapshots are stored in-region unless "cross-region-backup" is enabled (disabled by default).
- Isolation: Tenancy is enforced at the host and storage layers via tenant-id namespaces (LVM-like scoping for block volumes) + network ACLs; we include a diagram (segregation_diagram_v2.pdf) that shows network and storage boundaries.
- Wipe: The purge process is multi-stage:
  1) Mark tenant tombstone in control plane (instant)
  2) Drain active KV caches and invalidate prefixes (seconds to minutes depending on cache size)
  3) Queue block-volume zeroing and logical delete (parallel background jobs; window depends on volume size — typical: 30-180 minutes)
  4) Snapshot deletion and compaction (if any snapshots exist) — can take longer if snapshots are large or retained in cold storage; our default snapshot retention for Dedicated starts at 7 days but is configurable.

Expected wall-clock (typical dedicated customer profile):
- Small tenant (100GB active, no snapshots): full purge ~45-90 minutes.
- Medium tenant (1TB + single snapshot): ~3-6 hours.
- Large tenant with multiple snapshots and cold backups: variable; plan for up to 48 hours.

Audit artifacts produced:
- real-time event stream (tenant_tombstone, cache_invalidate, volume_delete_job_started/finished) — we can provide a sample audit log (attached sample_audit_log.csv)
- post-action attestation PDF with timestamps and operator IDs for exception workflows

Erase scenarios matrix (high level):
- Standard wipe: will remove live volumes and manifests; snapshots deleted as per retention; operator kicks off purge, TTLs applied; lower RTO/RPO.
- Emergency legal hold: purge is blocked; we mark hold and generate hold-specific audit events; operator must escalate to compliance to release.
- Snapshot-only removal: operator can target snapshots only (fast, minutes to hours)

Limitations / caveats:
- If customer has enabled cross-region backups, deletion of those copies is a separate job and may require coordination (we document it in the runbook).
- If a legal hold is in effect, purge is not automatic — we record the hold and provide evidence of blocked actions.

Attachments: segregation_diagram_v2.pdf, wipe_runbook_v1.docx, sample_audit_log.csv

If useful, we can provide a short anonymized playbook run (screen-recorded ops window + logs) as an addendum for your auditors.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Ben/Priya — thanks, this is helpful. A couple of clarifying questions from our InfraSec team: 

1) In the case of scheduled snapshots that were accidentally replicated off-region (operator error), is there an automated cross-region purge path or do we need to raise a support ticket? What evidence do you produce to show off-region copies were removed?

2) For the cache invalidation step, are the invalidation events flushed to the event stream before we mark the tenant as "complete"? We need to ensure there are no lingering in-memory prefixes that could be rehydrated in future restores.

3) Can you provide an example of the post-action attestation PDF (even redacted) and specify whether it includes operator biographical id (username) and the exact timestamps with timezone?

We may need a short addendum to the contract referencing the erase SLA for Dedicated. If we can get the sample attestation and a brief statement that cross-region is opt-in only, that'll cover our compliance board.

Cheers,
Chris

Subject: Re: Geo-lock verification and tenant segregation — attestation sample and procedures

Chris — attached is a redacted attestation sample (we include operator username, UTC timestamps, and job IDs). Notes below: 

1) Cross-region accidental replication: we have an automated discovery job that flags copies outside the tenant's pinned region. Deletion of those copies is an automated workflow if the cross-region-backup feature was disabled but a copy exists due to historical configuration; otherwise deletion is gated (requires customer approval) — we document this in the runbook. Evidence of removal is the volume_delete_job_started/finished events in the audit stream plus snapshot manifest removals; we can provide a signed attestation for the deletion job.

2) Cache invalidation: invalidation events are emitted synchronously as part of the purge transaction and appear in the event stream before the tenant_tombstone is marked complete. We also run a post-purge verification sweep that samples KV prefixes to confirm zero hits.

3) Attestation sample: the PDF includes
   - tenant_id, operator_username (redacted in shared copy), job_id, UTC timestamps (ISO 8601) for each stage, and a checksum of the manifest deleted.

We will upload the redacted attestation and a brief cross-region purge addendum to the Drive link (https://drive.redwood.com/FinTrust/geo-lock-evidence). If you want this baked into the contract we can draft a short SLA clause referencing our erase workflow and typical durations (we'll pass that to Legal).

Attachments: redacted_attestation_sample.pdf

Regards,
Ben
